lessons_control.note: pre_lessons is each hunter's own sum before it read researcher_us/LESSONS.md. edge_resolve.py ranks it against the same realised move as the key, which is the only thing that can tell the guidance file apart from a habit.

language_control.note: RETIRED 2026-09-22: the European and Canadian hunters now run one bilingual pass and emit no freeze, so this is 0/0 on every run sealed after that date. On earlier runs pre_local is each hunter's own sum after the ENGLISH pass and before the local pass; eu_resolve.py ranks it against the same realised move as the key, per market, and does not pool the UK (where the second pass varied source locality) with Germany and France (where it varied language).

note: Ranked on impact_sum: the hunters' signed per-finding sizes, added up, in points of spot. No call and no threshold -- cut wherever you like afterwards, which is what keeps the ranking question answerable at every k. `conviction` (abs of the key) is where the direction skill lives: over all events the sign is a coin flip, above the median conviction it is 74%. conviction_floor is a floor on emphasis in the note, never a filter on this file. Everything under `diagnostics` was measured as neutral or subtractive and decides nothing -- see researcher_us/EDGE_ANALYSIS.md.

Earnings Whispers says the Street 'bets beyond guidance'. If the print reiterates '50%+' without lifting it, the stock may read that as below the top-end models. findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2025-05-06 print fell 13.8% (a guide-driven reaction). The Q1 2026 guide raise drew +40.4%. Guidance has driven the large moves on this name.

findings.finding: Funding: UBS estimates DOCN needs about $4bn of incremental capital through mid-2029 to reach about 300 MW. The 10-Q shows $2.76bn of uncommenced co-location leases starting July 2026 to June 2028, $312.3m of 2026 converts due 2026-12-01 (conversion price $178.51, out of the money, so a cash repayment), cash of $767.0m and $406.7m of undrawn revolver at June 30. DOCN raised equity twice in 2026 ($888m follow-on in March, a 12.5m-share direct offering at $117.54 in July). What the money buys is answered: RPO of $894m (more than 10x a year earlier), 155 MW committed, and the $725m (+$300m accordion) equipment facility of 2026-09-11 funds 2027-28 capacity. So this is funding of visible demand, not distress. The residual risk is an equity or convert offering announced with or just after the print, at a price $26 below the July offering.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: April 2026: shares slid on the upsized ~$800m offering (QuiverQuant). July 2026 direct offering at $117.54, alongside the note repurchase. The August 2025 convert offering: shares -10% intraday.

findings.finding: The October drawdown is identified as sector contagion rather than company news. Neocloud credit stress (CoreWeave CDS at distress levels, CoreWeave -36% in October, Nebius about -27%), Musk's 2026-10-26 'guppy-level death' remark and Microsoft's 2026-10-28 capex below estimates all hit the group. DOCN fell -8.5% on 2026-10-14 on volume 91% below average and -10.1% on 2026-10-16, with no company release. DOCN's AI customer ARR is $234m of $1,125m total ARR (about 21%), so most of the business is the core developer cloud, which these credit fears do not touch. The print is the first company data point since the scare.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print came off a sector-driven drawdown of this size. The 2025-11-05 print (+18.0%) came after an AI-bubble scare in tech.

findings.finding: Counterparties that reported after DOCN last spoke show inference and cloud demand still ahead of supply, and GPU pricing rising. AWS Q3 2026 revenue grew +39% (its sixth straight quarter of acceleration). Azure grew +48%, with Microsoft saying demand exceeds capacity. Nebius raised on-demand H100/H200/B200/B300 prices 17-21% from 2026-10-01. That is a proxy positive for DOCN's AI ARR and on-demand GPU pricing, which matters for the Q4 guide (exit growth 35%+).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: DOCN's 2026 guide raises (Q1, Q2) came alongside AI ARR growth (+212% in Q2). The Q1 raise drew +40%.

findings.finding: Capacity-delivery risk, the swing factor UBS named for Q3. UBS (July 2026) said Richmond was near full and that the Kansas City MKC1 ramp was the key Q3 revenue swing. MKC1 then had a critical incident on 2026-08-19: about 8.5 hours of DOKS GPU nodes NotReady and inference endpoints unavailable, with GPU Droplets impacted beyond resolution and affected customers contacted directly. Microsoft's 2026-10-28 commentary says partners are taking longer to deliver data-center capacity. Any slip in the 155 MW schedule would weigh on Q4 and 2027 more than on Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not observed on a print. The company has said capacity came 'on or ahead of schedule' (2026-08-04 8-K).

findings.finding: RPO lumpiness and concentration. Q2 RPO was $893.8m ($365.9m within 12 months), driven by multiple nine-figure deals. The top 25 customers were about 20% of Q2 revenue against 9% a year earlier, and customers over $1M a month were 23%. Earnings Whispers flags that management calls RPO lumpy and that a flat or lower figure 'would need explanation'. Q2 also set a record of $93m new ARR, a high comparison for Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2026-07-07 RPO pre-release (above $800m) drew +4.3%. RPO has been bought when it jumped. No print yet has shown flat RPO.

findings.finding: The 2030 convertible notes ($625m, conversion price $39.17, deep in the money) were convertible at holders' option until 2026-09-30. About $153m of principal stayed outstanding after the 2026-07-23 repurchase of $471.8m, which is up to about 3.9m shares of possible Q3 conversions. The Q3 diluted share guide is about 126-127m.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None observed.

outside_window.finding: $312.3m of 2026 convertible notes mature on 2026-12-01 (conversion price $178.51, so a cash repayment). The cash covers it ($767m at June 30), but the repayment dates after the window.

lessons_applied: Lesson 4 (financing is a question): the money funds visible demand ($894m RPO, 155 MW committed, the $725m equipment facility), so the funding finding moved from -0.5 to -0.25. The only residual is the risk of an in-window offering.
Lesson 3 (caveat reaches the number): the 2027-bar finding moved from -1.0 to -0.5, net of the CFO's 2026-09-11 'highly confident in our outlook for 2027'.

Lesson 5 (proxies small, the drawdown cause is not evidence): the sector-contagion positioning finding moved from +0.5 to +0.25, the hyperscaler/GPU-pricing proxy from +0.75 to +0.5, and the Microsoft capacity-delivery read-through from -0.5 to -0.25.
Lesson 7 (sign against skew): p_up moved from 57 to 56 for the 8.3-point put skew; abs_move stays at 14.

Lessons 1, 6 and 9 left standing: the bar is sourced to the guide plus two agreeing estimates, the reaction history shows beats bought (6 of 8 up), and the AI share of ARR (~21%) is noted in the proxy finding.

findings.finding: The FY26 guide was explicitly conditioned on 'category price levels remain stabilized at current levels' (Aug 6 deck, slide 18). That deck's USDA wholesale chart had large white near ~$1.45/dz and rising at week 31. USDA's Egg Markets Overview of Oct 30, 2026 shows national loose large white at $0.35/dz, NY cartoned formula at $0.72/dz and breaking stock at $0.08/dz. VITL sells its excess eggs into the breaker channel, which cost it $19.5M of gross profit in Q2, and a lower conventional price widens its retail price gap. The stated condition for the guide has therefore failed. Revenue consensus ($763.8M) is already below the guide low ($775M), but the Street's FY EPS (-$0.38, implying positive H2 EPS concentrated in Q4) still sits inside the $0-10M EBITDA guide. The exposed number is a cut to the EBITDA or Q4 outlook.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guidance line is what has moved this stock. The Q1 2026 print with a sharp FY cut went -20.67% (2026-05-07). Q4 2025 (2026-02-26), with a weak guide, went -10.81%. Q2 2026, with the guide reaffirmed, went only +2.21% (2026-08-06). Guide raises in 2025 went +17.59% and +16.13%.

findings.finding: Competitive promotion inside VITL's own tier: USDA's Oct 30 report says 'non-organic free-range and pastured shell eggs continue to be the highest featured among the retail chains'. Pastured brown eggs were featured in 4,236 stores at an average ad price of $5.59/dz and free-range brown in 1,951 stores at $4.61. VITL's own Q2 ARP was $8.16 per EQ unit. The FY guide also assumes 'competitive activity does not intensify further' (Q2 release), and VITL launched its own sub-$5 free-range pilot at Target on Oct 23. Both point to continued pressure on price gaps and price/mix into Q4.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Widening price gaps and competitor promotions were the stated cause of the Q1 2026 miss and cut (-20.67%). The Q2 narrowing of the price gaps came with the guide reaffirmed (+2.21%).

findings.finding: Peer read-through: Cal-Maine's quarter ended Aug 29, 2026 (reported Sep 30) shows specialty shell egg sales -14.0%, with average selling price per dozen -10.7% and volume -3.8%. Specialty segment operating profit fell to $14.9M from $64.2M. Management still called specialty demand 'constructive'. This covers two of the three months of VITL's Q3 and points to continued price/mix deflation in specialty eggs. Q2 VITL revenue was -10.1% YoY; the $182.3M Q3 bar requires sequential growth of about 10% from $166.0M.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Pure revenue surprises have moved VITL less than guidance. Q2 2026 beat its revenue estimate ($166.0M against ~$160-170M, depending on source) and went +2.21%.

findings.finding: VITL's own Circana data, re-published in its September 2026 investor deck, shows Q3 entering with momentum. Average weekly volume per store selling per item was 27 in the 4 weeks to 7/19, the highest since February and +12.5% from April. At a top-10 retailer the price gap fell to $0.27 from $1.79, with velocity +27% and new households +27.2%. The deck reaffirms full-year TDPs of 150-160 and a Q4 average of 170-175, against 148.7 year to date through Q2. That supports Q3 revenue clearing the $182.3M bar on volume, even with price deflation.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 came with a revenue beat and these same velocity slides and went +2.21%. This name has not paid much for revenue beats when the guide was not raised.

findings.finding: Financing, and what it buys: Q2 cash was $21.2M with $30.0M of debt, H1 operating cash flow was -$45.9M, and H1 capex was $37.5M against a $70-75M FY guide. In August the company replaced its revolver with a $125M 3-year term loan and a $60M ABL, and terminated the buyback (Aug 3). The money funds capex already being slowed (VXR and accelerator farms) and operating losses, not a demand ramp: volume is declining. I found no covenant-pressure or going-concern language. The Q3 10-Q will show how much of the term loan was drawn.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The facility was announced with Q2 (+2.21%). The market did not treat it as distress.

findings.finding: The farm network quietly shrank: the Aug 6 deck said '625+ small farms, 10M+ birds'. The Oct 14 campaign release says 'more than 600' and the Oct 23 release says 'works with 600 small farms'. That is consistent with the farmer contract amendments and supply right-sizing management described. Less supply means fewer eggs dumped into the $0.08/dz breaker channel, which supports gross margin against the oversupply cost that hit Q2.

findings.finding: Defensive governance: on Aug 11, 2026 the board adopted amended bylaws that expand advance-notice disclosure for stockholder nominations and proposals, add director-candidate eligibility standards and add emergency bylaws (8-K filed Aug 17, 8-K/A to add the Item 5.03 label). Boards usually do this when they anticipate a nomination fight or an approach. Combined with a stock down ~75%, an activist or a strategic announcement at the print is possible but not evidenced. No 13D has been filed since July.
